The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 48 from LD Chandimal, complemented by a commanding 63-run stand between N Dickwella and LD Chandimal that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.55 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Kuldeep Yadav (4/40), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 135/10 (37.4 ov), Sri Lanka's innings completed the first-innings exchange (352 Runs (India)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Pallekele International Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 487/10 (122.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 135/10 (37.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 4-Wicket Spell: R Ashwin (4/68), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, HH Pandya delivered a masterclass for India (108 Runs & 1 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 63%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by R Ashwin (31 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by innings & 171 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
